{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABdNxEtg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhGvLEk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 6, "title": "feat: implement Cognix MVP v0.1 end-to-end", "body": "## Problem

The [MVP v0.1 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/mvp.md) is merged, but Cognix currently has no executable application, agent harness, or tests. We need a working, verifiable first release rather than a prototype that only chats with a local model.

**This Issue tracks complete MVP implementation.** All requirements in F1–F7 and acceptance scenarios S1–S6 are in scope. It must remain open until their mandatory acceptance is satisfied; design sketches, scaffold-only work, or partial implementations do not resolve it.

## Expected outcome

A user can start Cognix in a local project from a terminal, choose an Ollama model, instruct it to fix a small bug, review/approve proposed changes and verification commands, and receive an evidence-based result. Cognix must safely and autonomously repeat the **model → tool call → authorized execution → tool result → model** cycle within explicit bounds.

Illustrative workflow (the commands do not exist yet):

```sh
cd example-project
cognix --model qwen3.8:27b
# > Fix the division-by-zero bug in main.py and verify the result.
```

Use **Ollama** as the initial inference provider. **Qwen3.8 27B** is the first evaluation target, subject to actual availability and tool-calling compatibility checks, **not** a hard-coded dependency. Accept other compatible Ollama model tags (including suitable DeepSeek models) at startup via `--model` and a configurable default. Additional provider integrations are not required in v0.1.

### Implementation scope (aligned to docs/mvp.md)

- **F1 — CLI:** Working terminal entry point for one selected project root; natural-language user input, visible tool activity, clear final results/errors, approval interactions, and user cancellation. A simple CLI is sufficient.
- **F2 — Model provider:** Functional Ollama chat/tool-calling integration through a narrow, replaceable interface. Validate server/model availability and tool-calling behavior; surface actionable failures without silently proceeding. Normal inference must not require a hosted AI API.
- **F3 — Agent loop:** Supply instructions, tool definitions, and current conversation context; interpret and validate tool calls; execute authorized calls; return structured tool outputs (including errors) to the model; continue or stop on final answer, cancellation, limit, or unrecoverable error. Limit iteration and prevent uncontrolled loops.
- **F4 — Four tools:** Implement `list_files`, `read_file`, `apply_patch` (targeted changes, with patch preview), and `run_command` (bounded verification execution). Validate inputs and report failure precisely.
- **F5 — Context:** Maintain user input, model outputs, tool calls, and tool results within an in-memory session. Handle context overflow explicitly without silently losing essential information.
- **F6 — Safety:** Check real/canonical project-root boundaries and symlink escapes; prevent outside-root reads/writes; show diffs and require approval before file changes; require approval before commands; enforce an explicit verification-command policy or suitable isolation (approval alone is not a sandbox); bound command time/output; cancel running work; preserve existing user changes.
- **F7 — Outcome reporting:** Report modified files, exact checks actually executed and their outcomes, failures, denials, cancellation and unrun checks. Never claim that tests passed without evidence.

### Proposed implementation sequence (not independent completion criteria)

1. Select and document the smallest appropriate implementation language/libraries (Rust is a candidate), project layout, and executable build/run/test commands.
2. Implement the model adapter, CLI model selection, and deterministic mocked-provider test harness.
3. Implement the agent loop, in-memory context, tool-call schema validation, and termination paths.
4. Implement the four tools plus path/approval/command-policy boundaries.
5. Integrate end-to-end CLI, cancellation, actionable errors, and evidence-based reporting.
6. Run fixture-based regression/security tests and actual local Ollama evaluation, document results, review, and merge.

Keep shared agent logic separate from the CLI enough to permit a desktop frontend later, without building desktop infrastructure now. Prefer the smallest cohesive design that meets the requirements; don't add speculative abstractions.

## Context and reproduction

- Canonical scope and scenarios: [docs/mvp.md](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/mvp.md) (F1–F7, S1–S6).
- Long-term vision: [Issue #3](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/issues/3). MVP specification task: [Issue #4](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/issues/4) (completed).
- Reference implementation: [OpenAI Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), for agent-loop/tool-routing concepts, not feature parity.
- Initial evaluation machine: Apple M4 Max, 64 GB unified memory.
- Follow the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review rules](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/cognix/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md).
- Reproduction: The application is not yet implemented. Confirm the actual repository state before editing.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

All of the following are required for **complete resolution of this implementation Issue**. Map each AC to implementation locations and actual evidence at the current PR head.

- [ ] **AC1 — Executable CLI (F1):** A clean checkout builds/starts using documented commands. A user can start an interactive session from a local project, provide a task, see progress and final results, respond to approvals, and interrupt work. Verify successful startup, invalid inputs and interrupted interaction.
- [ ] **AC2 — Selectable local model (F2, S5):** Ollama connection works with an explicit `--model` and documented default; the harness does not hard-code Qwen3.8. Missing Ollama, missing model and unsupported tool-calling behavior produce clear errors. Verify with deterministic mock responses and a real compatible local model, recording the exact tag and provider version. Test Qwen3.8 27B availability/compatibility rather than assuming it.
- [ ] **AC3 — Agent loop and context (F3, F5, S1):** Model-chosen valid tool calls execute and results return into the next model request. Message/tool-call ordering and call IDs are preserved. A no-tool final answer terminates normally; malformed calls, failed tools, context-limit errors, cancellation, step exhaustion and unrecoverable failures have bounded, observable behavior. Add automated tests with mock model responses.
- [ ] **AC4 — Four tools (F4):** `list_files`, `read_file`, `apply_patch` and `run_command` operate on small project fixtures; patch changes are shown before approval, targeted to requested files, and failures are returned as structured results. Add success, invalid-argument and failure-path tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Safety and control (F6, S4):** Verify out-of-root and symlink traversal are denied; approval denial executes nothing; commands cannot bypass the documented execution policy/isolation; cancel stops running execution and prevents subsequent steps; step/time/output limits hold; unrelated/pre-existing changes are preserved. Include adversarial fixture cases, not only happy paths.
- [ ] **AC6 — End-to-end edit/verify/recovery (F3, F4, F7, S2, S3):** On a reproducible division-by-zero fixture, the agent reads relevant code, proposes and applies an **approved** patch, runs **approved** validation, and reports results. Given a failed check, it can try a bounded correction or truthfully explain the blocker. Test control flow deterministically and record actual-model trials separately (attempts, successes and failures; no assumed 100% success).
- [ ] **AC7 — Accurate reporting (F7):** Verify reporting distinguishes passed, failed, not run, denied, canceled and limit-reached outcomes. A tool error, skipped test or refused command must never be represented as a successful verification.
- [ ] **AC8 — Reproducible documentation and checks (S6):** Update README/developer documentation with real prerequisites, setup, run/build/test commands, sample workflow, model/provider compatibility limitations, security/approval behavior, and recorded validation results. Include the exact model tag, Ollama version, fixture and hardware when reporting local trials. Run applicable formatting, unit/integration and documentation checks and report **Pass / Fail / Skipped / Not run** honestly.

### Review and completion policy

Review the full implemented scope against every AC at the latest PR head. If work spans multiple PRs, each must have a clearly scoped result and follow the existing repository authorization/review rules; use non-closing references until **all AC1–AC8** are satisfied. Do not close this Issue merely because a scaffold or a subset of components was merged. Do not assert that external hardware/model validation has occurred without recorded evidence; record concrete blockers if unavailable.

## Validation already performed

**Pass:** Read the current MVP specification, repository development guidance and Issue template; verified that the current repository root contains guidance and docs but no application manifest or executable agent.

**Not run:** Application build, tests, Ollama runtime/model integration, actual CLI trials, and diff checks: implementation does not exist yet. These checks must be performed on the implementation.

## Optional validation

- Compare agent behavior against Codex on equivalent small fixtures, where practical.
- Measure token use, wall-clock time, and memory for repeat trials; establish thresholds only from observed evidence.
- Evaluate a second compatible Ollama model (e.g. a DeepSeek variant) beyond the minimum model-selection contract.

These are useful, but not additional completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required by default; all required implementation and verification evidence is intended to be obtained before final merge. If a genuinely merge-only check emerges, document why it cannot run earlier and track it explicitly without treating it as pre-merge evidence.
